board_events.text: The shoot tip is an AUXIN FACTORY. Auxin streams downward from it and SUPPRESSES the lateral buds below - a phenomenon called APICAL DOMINANCE.

Remove the tip (decapitation) and you cut off the auxin supply. The freed lateral buds burst into growth, and a single leggy stem becomes a dense, branching hedge. This is exactly the trick used in tea plantations and hedge-making.
A perfect illustration of a hormone controlling FORM by where it is made and which growth it switches off.

Limiting condition: the 'promoter vs inhibitor' labels are useful, not absolute. Ethylene is the classic rule-breaker - it promotes ripening, pineapple flowering and root-hair growth, yet it also drives senescence and abscission.

A hormone's effect depends on CONCENTRATION, TISSUE TYPE and the presence of OTHER hormones. The same dose of auxin that promotes shoot growth can inhibit root growth. Never quote a hormone's effect without its context.

segments.text: An assertion-reason question, N E E T high-difficulty, and I want to teach the method here as much as the answer. Assertion-reason is three questions in disguise, and you must ask all three in order.
Assertion A: in plants, two cells produced by the very same meristem can mature into structurally different cell types. Hold that, and do not judge it yet.

Reason R: plant differentiation is open, so the final structure depends on the cell's position and on environmental signals, rather than being fixed at birth. Now we have both statements. Three questions follow. Is A true? Is R true? And - the one people skip - does R explain A?

Look at the diagram while we work. One meristem at the top, sister cells identical at birth, and two arrows going to two different positions. On the left, a tracheary element - protoplasm lost, thick lignified wall, a hollow dead water pipe. On the right, a completely different cell type - protoplasm kept, thin wall, alive and working. Same origin, same genes, two fates.
Question one: is A true? Yes. It is not just true, it is the defining feature of plant differentiation - the picture shows exactly that. Sisters from one meristem ending up structurally different.
Question two: is R true? Yes. Differentiation being open is precisely what the chapter states, and it is why position and environment can steer a cell's fate. So both statements stand.

Question three, and this is where the marks actually are. Does R explain A? Yes - and think about why. Because differentiation is open, meaning not pre-programmed at birth, the cell's fate is left to be decided later, by where it sits and what the environment demands. That is the mechanism by which siblings can diverge. R is the cause; A is the consequence. R does not merely sit next to A - it produces A.
So the answer is option one: both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

<whisper>And the trap, which is a beautiful one. Students who have memorised open differentiation as a label - who can say the phrase but have never connected it to a cause - will mark both statements true and then downgrade to option two, R not the explanation. They lose the mark not on the facts, but on the link. In assertion-reason, always ask the third question out loud.
Let us finish this subtopic with the four places students actually lose these marks. Not the content again - the failure modes. Each one is a specific, repeatable mistake, and each one is avoidable.

Pitfall one, and it is the deadliest: absolute growth rate is not relative growth rate. Two organs with identical absolute growth can have wildly different relative growth - we just saw one hundred percent against ten percent from the same four centimetres. The tell is in the question paper: whenever it hands you two initial sizes, it is setting up the R G R comparison. Two starting sizes is never decoration.

Pitfall two: the scrambled developmental order. Students flip differentiation and maturation, or they push senescence too early in the chain. Lock the sequence and do not negotiate with it. Divide, enlarge, differentiate, mature, senesce, die. And if you ever doubt it, rebuild it from logic - nothing can specialise before it exists, nothing can age before it has matured.

Pitfall three: the de- versus re-differentiation mix-up. Say it as two directions, not two names. Dedifferentiation restores division, and it makes a meristem. Redifferentiation removes division again, and it makes a final tissue. So the cambium is born by dedifferentiation and yields tissues by redifferentiation. One process for each direction - if a question describes a cell gaining division, it is de, no matter what structure is mentioned.

Pitfall four: calling all plant growth indeterminate. It is a slogan and it is mostly right, which is exactly what makes it dangerous. Leaves, flowers and fruits are determinate - they stop at a set size. The plant as a whole keeps going; its individual organs do not. Do not over-generalise.

Now the pro-tip, and this one is a genuine time-saver in the exam. For A G R and R G R questions, do not start computing decimals. Glance at the initial sizes first. The organ that starts smaller will almost always win on R G R, even when the A G R is equal - because it is the same numerator divided by a smaller number.

That instant ratio-sense lets you eliminate two options before you touch a calculator. In a paper where seconds matter, that is the difference between attempting the last question and not. Read, glance at the starting sizes, eliminate, then compute only if you must.

<excited>And carry the two mnemonics out with you, because between them they cover most of this subtopic. For the order: Di - El - Di - Ma - Se. Division, Elongation, Differentiation, Maturation, Senescence. And for the direction: DE equals Division Enabled, RE equals Retired again. Two lines, and a large chunk of a near-guaranteed N E E T question is already answered.

<curious>Start with something genuinely strange. A plant has no brain. No nerves. No muscles. And yet a root knows to grow down while the shoot grows up. A banana decides to ripen. A tree decides to drop its leaves before winter. Who is giving the orders?

Because there is nobody in there. No control room, no signal running down a nerve. And yet the decisions get made, reliably, in the right order, in the right season. That is the puzzle this subtopic exists to solve.

The answer is chemistry. Plants run their entire lives on a small set of chemical messengers called plant growth regulators - P G Rs - also known as phytohormones. Think of them as text messages. Tiny. Made in one part of the plant, carried to another, and capable of switching enormous processes on or off.

Two features make them remarkable, and both are exam-relevant. First, they work in astonishingly small amounts - a few molecules can swing the fate of a whole organ. Second, they are chemically diverse. There is no single hormone formula. Auxins are indole compounds. Gibberellins are terpenes. Cytokinins are adenine, or purine, derivatives. Abscisic acid is a carotenoid derivative. And ethylene is a simple gas.

So look at the picture, because it shows how biologists handle that chemical zoo. They gave up on sorting hormones by what they are made of, and sorted them by what they do instead. Two pans on a see-saw.

Here is the analogy to hold. Think of the plant's life as a car. The promoters - auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins - are the accelerator: they drive cell division, cell enlargement, flowering, fruiting and the breaking of dormancy. The inhibitors - abscisic acid and, in many of its roles, ethylene - are the brake: they slow things down, enforce dormancy, close stomata and trigger ageing.

But do not picture a plant as either accelerating or braking. A healthy plant is feathering both pedals, constantly. Growth is never about one hormone winning. It is about the balance and the ratio between them, at a given place and at a given time.

And I am marking that in red because it is the single most important takeaway of this subtopic. The same tissue, given a different ratio of the same two hormones, will do completely different things. We will make that precise later with the famous auxin-to-cytokinin story - but carry the idea from right now.
Before we open the textbook list, I want you to notice that you have already seen this chemistry working - probably without knowing it.

You have watched a gardener pinch off the growing tip of a hedge. Just the tip, with fingers or shears. And the result is not a shorter hedge - it is a denser, bushier one. Now that is a strange outcome if you think about it. You removed growth and got more growth. That is hormone chemistry, done with fingertips.
Look at the two panels. Left, the intact shoot. Right, the same plant with the tip pinched off. Watch what happens to the little lateral buds down the side in each case.

Here is the mechanism. The shoot tip is an auxin factory. Auxin is made there, and it streams downward from the tip - and as it passes, it suppresses the lateral buds sitting below. They are alive, they are capable, and they are being held back chemically. That suppression has a name: apical dominance. The apex dominates, and the sides stay quiet.

So now remove the tip. Decapitation, as the chapter calls it. You have not touched the lateral buds at all - but you have cut off their auxin supply. The suppression lifts. The freed lateral buds burst into growth, and a single leggy stem becomes a dense, branching hedge. That is exactly the trick used in tea plantations and in hedge-making.

Sit with what that shows. The gardener never told the plant to branch. He simply removed the source of a chemical instruction. The hormone was controlling the plant's form by where it was made and by which growth it switched off. Shape, from chemistry and geometry.

Now an important warning before the lists arrive. The promoter versus inhibitor labels are useful, but they are not absolute. Ethylene is the classic rule-breaker. It promotes fruit ripening, flowering in pineapple, and root-hair growth - all promoter-like. Yet it also drives senescence and abscission - firmly inhibitor-like. One hormone, both camps.

<whisper>And the deeper rule, which is where careless answers die. A hormone's effect depends on concentration, on tissue type, and on which other hormones are present. The very same dose of auxin that promotes shoot growth can inhibit root growth. So never quote a hormone's effect without its context. State the role and the situation, not just the label.
एक assertion-reason question, N E E T high-difficulty, और मैं यहाँ answer जितना ही method सिखाना चाहती हूँ। Assertion-reason असल में तीन सवाल हैं भेस बदल कर, और तीनों को order में पूछना ज़रूरी है।
Assertion A: plants में, एक ही meristem से बने दो cells structurally अलग cell types में mature हो सकते हैं। इसे पकड़ रखिए, अभी judge मत कीजिए।

Reason R: plant differentiation open है, इसलिए final structure cell की position और environmental signals पर depend करता है, जन्म के समय fix नहीं होता। अब दोनों statements हमारे पास हैं। तीन सवाल आते हैं। A सही है? R सही है? और - जो लोग छोड़ देते हैं - क्या R, A को explain करता है?

काम करते हुए diagram देखिए। ऊपर एक meristem, जन्म पर identical sister cells, और दो arrows दो अलग positions की तरफ़। बाएँ एक tracheary element - protoplasm ख़त्म, मोटी lignified wall, एक hollow dead water pipe. दाएँ बिलकुल दूसरा cell type - protoplasm बचा हुआ, पतली wall, ज़िंदा और काम करता हुआ। एक ही origin, एक ही genes, दो fates.
पहला सवाल: A सही है? हाँ। सिर्फ़ सही नहीं, ये plant differentiation का defining feature है - picture ठीक यही दिखा रही है। एक meristem की sisters structurally अलग निकल रही हैं।
दूसरा सवाल: R सही है? हाँ। Differentiation का open होना बिलकुल वही है जो chapter कहता है, और इसीलिए position और environment cell की fate steer कर सकते हैं। तो दोनों statements खड़े हैं।

तीसरा सवाल, और असली marks यहीं हैं। क्या R, A को explain करता है? हाँ - और सोचिए क्यों। क्योंकि differentiation open है, यानी जन्म पर pre-programmed नहीं, cell की fate बाद के लिए छोड़ दी जाती है - ये तय होता है कि वो बैठा कहाँ है और environment क्या माँग रहा है। यही वो mechanism है जिससे siblings अलग हो सकते हैं। R cause है; A consequence. R सिर्फ़ A के बगल में खड़ा नहीं है - वो A को पैदा करता है।
तो answer है option one: A और R दोनों सही, और R, A का correct explanation है।

<whisper>और trap, जो बड़ा ख़ूबसूरत है। जिन students ने open differentiation को सिर्फ़ label की तरह रटा है - जो phrase बोल सकते हैं पर उसे कभी cause से नहीं जोड़ा - वो दोनों statements true mark करके option two पर उतर आते हैं, कि R explanation नहीं है। Marks facts पर नहीं, link पर जाते हैं। Assertion-reason में तीसरा सवाल हमेशा ज़ोर से पूछिए।
इस subtopic को उन चार जगहों के साथ ख़त्म करते हैं जहाँ students असल में marks गँवाते हैं। Content दोबारा नहीं - failure modes. हर एक एक specific, बार-बार होने वाली ग़लती है, और हर एक टल सकती है।

पहला pitfall, और सबसे जानलेवा: absolute growth rate, relative growth rate नहीं है। बराबर absolute growth वाले दो organs का relative growth ज़मीन-आसमान अलग हो सकता है - अभी उन्हीं चार centimetres से one hundred percent बनाम ten percent देखा। इशारा question paper में ही है: जब भी वो दो initial sizes दे, वो R G R comparison बिछा रहा है। दो starting sizes कभी decoration नहीं होते।

दूसरा pitfall: scrambled developmental order. Students differentiation और maturation उलट देते हैं, या senescence को chain में जल्दी खींच लाते हैं। Sequence lock कीजिए और उससे मोल-भाव मत कीजिए। Divide, enlarge, differentiate, mature, senesce, die. और कभी शक हो तो logic से दोबारा बना लीजिए - कोई चीज़ मौजूद हुए बिना specialise नहीं कर सकती, mature हुए बिना age नहीं कर सकती।

तीसरा pitfall: de बनाम re-differentiation का घालमेल। इसे दो नामों की तरह नहीं, दो directions की तरह बोलिए। Dedifferentiation division वापस लाता है, और meristem बनाता है। Redifferentiation division फिर से हटाता है, और final tissue बनाता है। तो cambium पैदा होता है dedifferentiation से और tissues देता है redifferentiation से। हर direction के लिए एक process - question में cell division पा रहा हो तो वो de है, चाहे कोई भी structure बताया गया हो।

चौथा pitfall: हर plant growth को indeterminate कह देना। ये slogan है और ज़्यादातर सही है, और यही इसे ख़तरनाक बनाता है। Leaves, flowers और fruits determinate हैं - एक set size पर रुक जाते हैं। पूरा plant चलता रहता है; उसके individual organs नहीं। Over-generalise मत कीजिए।

अब pro-tip, और ये exam में सच में time बचाता है। A G R और R G R के questions में decimals निकालना शुरू मत कीजिए। पहले initial sizes पर नज़र डालिए। जो organ छोटे से शुरू होता है वो R G R में लगभग हमेशा जीतेगा, चाहे A G R बराबर हो - क्योंकि वही numerator छोटे number से divide हो रहा है।

वही instant ratio-sense आपको calculator छूने से पहले दो options हटा देने देता है। जिस paper में seconds मायने रखते हैं, वहाँ यही फ़र्क है आख़िरी question attempt करने और छूट जाने के बीच। पढ़िए, starting sizes पर नज़र डालिए, eliminate कीजिए, और compute तभी जब ज़रूरी हो।

<excited>और दोनों mnemonics साथ लेकर जाइए, क्योंकि ये दोनों मिल कर इस subtopic का बड़ा हिस्सा ढक लेते हैं। Order के लिए: Di - El - Di - Ma - Se. Division, Elongation, Differentiation, Maturation, Senescence. और direction के लिए: DE equals Division Enabled, RE equals Retired again. दो lines, और एक near-guaranteed N E E T question का बड़ा हिस्सा पहले ही answer हो चुका है।

<curious>शुरुआत एक सच में अजीब बात से। Plant के पास brain नहीं है। Nerves नहीं। Muscles नहीं। और फिर भी root को पता है नीचे जाना है, shoot को ऊपर। Banana तय करता है कि पकना है। Tree तय करता है कि सर्दी से पहले पत्ते गिराने हैं। हुक्म दे कौन रहा है?

क्योंकि अंदर कोई है ही नहीं। न control room, न कोई signal जो nerve से दौड़े। और फिर भी फ़ैसले होते हैं, भरोसे के साथ, सही order में, सही मौसम में। यही पहेली है जिसे हल करने के लिए ये subtopic मौजूद है।

जवाब है chemistry. Plants अपनी पूरी life chemical messengers के एक छोटे से set पर चलाते हैं, जिन्हें plant growth regulators - P G Rs - कहते हैं, या phytohormones. इन्हें text messages समझिए। बहुत छोटे। Plant के एक हिस्से में बनते हैं, दूसरे तक जाते हैं, और बहुत बड़े processes को on या off कर सकते हैं।

दो features इन्हें remarkable बनाते हैं, और दोनों exam-relevant हैं। पहला, ये हैरान करने वाली छोटी मात्रा में काम करते हैं - चंद molecules पूरे organ की क़िस्मत पलट सकते हैं। दूसरा, ये chemically diverse हैं। कोई एक hormone formula है ही नहीं। Auxins indole compounds हैं। Gibberellins terpenes. Cytokinins adenine, यानी purine, derivatives. Abscisic acid एक carotenoid derivative. और ethylene एक simple gas.

तो picture देखिए, क्योंकि वो दिखाती है कि biologists ने इस chemical zoo को कैसे संभाला। उन्होंने hormones को उनकी बनावट से sort करना छोड़ दिया, और इस हिसाब से sort किया कि वो करते क्या हैं। See-saw पर दो pans.

ये रही पकड़ने वाली analogy. Plant की life को एक car समझिए। Promoters - auxins, gibberellins और cytokinins - accelerator हैं: वो cell division, cell enlargement, flowering, fruiting और dormancy तोड़ना चलाते हैं। Inhibitors - abscisic acid और, अपने कई roles में, ethylene - brake हैं: वो चीज़ें धीमी करते हैं, dormancy लागू करते हैं, stomata बंद करते हैं, और ageing शुरू करते हैं।

पर plant को ऐसे मत सोचिए कि वो या तो accelerate कर रहा है या brake लगा रहा है। एक healthy plant लगातार दोनों pedals feather कर रहा होता है। Growth कभी एक hormone के जीतने की बात नहीं है। ये balance और ratio की बात है, एक ख़ास जगह पर और एक ख़ास वक़्त पर।

और इसे मैं red में mark कर रही हूँ क्योंकि यही इस subtopic का सबसे ज़रूरी takeaway है। वही tissue, उन्हीं दो hormones का अलग ratio मिलने पर, बिलकुल अलग काम करेगा। इसे आगे मशहूर auxin-to-cytokinin कहानी से precise करेंगे - पर idea अभी से साथ रखिए।
Textbook की list खोलने से पहले मैं चाहती हूँ आप notice करें कि ये chemistry आप पहले ही काम करते हुए देख चुके हैं - शायद बिना जाने।

आपने gardener को hedge की growing tip चुटकी से तोड़ते देखा है। सिर्फ़ tip, उँगलियों या shears से। और नतीजा छोटी hedge नहीं होता - बल्कि घनी, bushy hedge होती है। सोचिए तो ये अजीब outcome है। आपने growth हटाई और ज़्यादा growth मिली। ये hormone chemistry है, उँगलियों से की हुई।
दोनों panels देखिए। बाएँ intact shoot. दाएँ वही plant, tip चुटकी से हटा कर। दोनों में side के छोटे lateral buds के साथ क्या होता है, उस पर नज़र रखिए।

ये रहा mechanism. Shoot tip एक auxin factory है। Auxin वहीं बनता है, और tip से नीचे की तरफ़ बहता है - और रास्ते में नीचे बैठे lateral buds को suppress करता जाता है। वो ज़िंदा हैं, वो सक्षम हैं, और उन्हें chemically रोका जा रहा है। इस suppression का नाम है apical dominance. Apex हुक्म चलाता है, और sides चुप रहती हैं।

तो अब tip हटा दीजिए। Decapitation, जैसा chapter कहता है। आपने lateral buds को छुआ तक नहीं - पर उनकी auxin supply काट दी। Suppression हट जाती है। आज़ाद हुए lateral buds फूट पड़ते हैं, और एक लंबा दुबला stem घनी, branching hedge बन जाता है। यही trick tea plantations और hedge-making में इस्तेमाल होती है।

इस पर ठहरिए कि ये दिखाता क्या है। Gardener ने plant से कभी नहीं कहा कि branch करो। उसने बस एक chemical instruction का source हटा दिया। Hormone plant की form control कर रहा था - इससे कि वो कहाँ बनता है, और किस growth को off रखता है। Chemistry और geometry से shape.

अब lists आने से पहले एक ज़रूरी warning. Promoter बनाम inhibitor labels काम के हैं, पर absolute नहीं। Ethylene classic rule-breaker है। वो fruit ripening promote करता है, pineapple में flowering, और root-hair growth - सब promoter-like. और फिर भी वो senescence और abscission भी चलाता है - पक्का inhibitor-like. एक hormone, दोनों camps.

<whisper>और गहरा rule, जहाँ लापरवाह answers दम तोड़ते हैं। Hormone का effect concentration पर, tissue type पर, और इस पर depend करता है कि और कौन से hormones मौजूद हैं। Auxin की वही dose जो shoot growth promote करती है, root growth inhibit कर सकती है। तो hormone का effect कभी बिना context के मत बोलिए। Role और situation बताइए, सिर्फ़ label नहीं।

sections.title: The definition, and regulator one: auxins & How auxin was discovered: a chain of reasoning

board_events.text: PGR: a trace-amount organic molecule that steers growth

PLANT GROWTH REGULATOR (PGR): a small organic molecule of diverse chemical composition that, in TRACE amounts, influences plant growth and development. Two functional groups - PROMOTERS (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins) and INHIBITORS (abscisic acid; ethylene in its inhibitory roles).
PGRs carry no formulae and no dimensions. This subtopic is descriptive - do not go hunting for equations.

board_events.text: AUXINS are indole compounds. Natural: IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) and IBA (indole-3-butyric acid). Synthetic: NAA (naphthalene acetic acid), 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid), 2,4,5-T.
Auxins are transported in a characteristic POLAR manner - one-way, from shoot tip towards the base.
Effects: cell elongation; apical dominance (suppresses lateral buds); root initiation in stem cuttings; promotes xylem differentiation; mediates phototropism.
Also: prevents abscission of YOUNG leaves and fruits, but promotes the fall of OLDER ones. Induces parthenocarpy - seedless fruit such as tomato, using dilute IAA or IBA.
Application: 2,4-D is a selective weedicide against broad-leaved (dicot) weeds.

board_events.text: GIBBERELLINS are terpene-based; the most studied is GA3. Their nature is ACIDIC.

GA effects: internode elongation - causing BOLTING, the rapid stem elongation before flowering in rosette plants; converts genetic dwarfs to tall; breaks seed and bud dormancy; promotes seed germination; speeds early seed production in conifers; induces alpha-amylase synthesis in germinating cereal grains.
GA applications: increases the length of grape stalks, enlarges fruit such as apple, and increases sugarcane yield.
CYTOKININS are adenine (purine) derivatives. Natural: ZEATIN, from maize kernels and coconut milk. Synthetic: KINETIN. Their nature is BASIC.

Cytokinin effects: promotes cell division (cytokinesis); helps OVERCOME apical dominance, promoting lateral shoot and bud growth; delays leaf senescence - the RICHMOND-LANG effect - by mobilising nutrients and controlling protein synthesis; promotes chloroplast development and nutrient mobilisation.
Where cytokinins live: sites of rapid, continuous cell division - root apices, developing shoot buds and young fruits.
Acid-base tags worth owning: gibberellins ACIDIC, cytokinins BASIC, abscisic acid ACIDIC.

board_events.text: ETHYLENE ($C_2H_4$) is a GASEOUS hormone - the only one. It is synthesised from the amino acid METHIONINE, and supplied commercially as ETHEPHON, which releases ethylene in tissue.

Ethylene effects: hastens fruit ripening (climacteric - it raises the respiration rate); promotes senescence and abscission of leaves and flowers; breaks seed and bud dormancy; promotes root-hair formation.
More ethylene: induces flowering and fruit-set synchronisation in pineapple and mango; increases the number of female flowers in cucurbits; used for fruit thinning in cotton, cherry and walnut.
ABSCISIC ACID (ABA) is a carotenoid derivative, precursor violaxanthin. Other names: abscisin II, and dormin. Nature: acidic - the general STRESS HORMONE.

ABA effects: promotes seed and bud DORMANCY; induces STOMATAL CLOSURE under water stress - accumulating in drought-stressed leaves, it makes the guard cells lose turgor, so the stomata shut and water is conserved; inhibits growth and metabolism.
ABA is ANTAGONISTIC to gibberellin: GA breaks dormancy, ABA enforces it. Learn them as a pair, not as two facts.
Despite its name, ABA is NOT the main driver of abscission - that owes more to the ethylene / auxin balance. ABA's headline jobs are dormancy and stomatal closure.
The founding experiment of plant hormone biology

board_events.text: Charles Darwin and his son Francis noticed that grass coleoptiles bend TOWARDS light. By covering different parts, they reasoned that the TIP perceives the light - yet the bending happens LOWER DOWN.
The inference: if the tip senses but the base bends, then a SIGNAL must travel from tip to growth zone. But what kind of signal?

Decades later, F. W. Went collected that signal by standing cut coleoptile tips on AGAR BLOCKS. The agar alone could then make a TIPLESS coleoptile bend - proving the signal was a DIFFUSIBLE CHEMICAL. That chemical is AUXIN.
The deeper mechanism: light drives auxin to the SHADED side. Extra auxin there means extra elongation, so the shaded side grows faster and the shoot bends toward the light.
Why this matters: it is the founding experiment of plant hormone biology, and a perennial C B S E and N E E T favourite.
Sourcing note: the Darwin step is grounded in the chapter; the Went step is the standard N C E R T account.

segments.text: Now the formal definition, and it is worth reading slowly because every clause earns its place. A plant growth regulator is a small organic molecule of diverse chemical composition that, in trace amounts, influences plant growth and development.

Take the clauses apart. Small organic molecule - so not a protein, not an enzyme. Of diverse chemical composition - that is the chemical zoo we met, written into the definition itself. In trace amounts - the potency. And influences growth and development - the job. Then the classification: two functional groups. Promoters, which are auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins. Inhibitors, which are abscisic acid, and ethylene in its inhibitory roles.

<curious>And one relief, which I want to say plainly because students arrive expecting the worst. P G Rs carry no formulae and no dimensions. This entire subtopic is descriptive. So do not go hunting for equations here - there are none to find. What is being tested is whether you know what each molecule does, and why.
So, regulator number one: auxins. Look at the card. Four compartments - natural, synthetic, transport, and effects - and every exam question lives in one of them.

Auxins are indole compounds. The natural ones are I A A, which is indole-three-acetic acid, and I B A, indole-three-butyric acid. The synthetic ones are N A A, naphthalene acetic acid, then two four D - full name two, four-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid - and two, four, five-T. And notice the pattern in the picture: both natural ones carry indole in the name. The synthetic ones do not. That is your mnemonic, and it is free.

Transport next, and auxin is unusual here. It moves in a characteristic polar manner. Polar means one-way - from the shoot tip towards the base, and not back again. That one-way street is what makes apical dominance possible, since it is exactly how the tip's auxin reaches the buds below it.

Now the effects, and read them as one story rather than a list. Cell elongation. Apical dominance, suppressing lateral buds - which we just did. Root initiation in stem cuttings. It promotes xylem differentiation. And it mediates phototropism, the bending toward light.

Two more, and the first is a trap. Auxin prevents abscission of young leaves and fruits - but promotes the fall of older ones. Same hormone, opposite outcomes, decided by the age of the organ. That is the context rule from the last section, made concrete. And finally it induces parthenocarpy - seedless fruit such as tomato, using dilute I A A or I B A.

The headline application, and it will come back in a worked example: two four D is a selective weedicide, used against broad-leaved dicot weeds. Note the word selective. It does not kill everything - and why it spares the crop is a question in its own right.
Two more promoters, and I want to teach them as a pair, because the exam almost always tests them together and because their jobs are complementary rather than overlapping.

Look at the two panels. Left, gibberellins. Right, cytokinins. Notice that each panel has the same four rows - chemistry, nature, effects, uses. Same skeleton, different flesh. If you learn one card's shape, you can fill in the other.

Gibberellins first. They are terpene-based, and the most studied one is G A three. Their nature is acidic - and that is a real exam detail, not decoration, because the acid-base tags get asked directly.

Now the effects, and here is the organising idea: gibberellin's signature move is making things longer. Internode elongation is the core, and that causes bolting - the rapid stem elongation before flowering in rosette plants. Look at the little diagram: a squat rosette on the left, and after G A three, a tall bolted stem. It converts genetic dwarfs to tall. It breaks seed and bud dormancy, and promotes seed germination. It speeds early seed production in conifers. And it induces alpha-amylase synthesis in germinating cereal grains.

The applications follow directly from that one idea, longer. It increases the length of grape stalks. It enlarges fruit, such as apple. And it increases sugarcane yield - and think about why that works. Sugarcane stores its sugar in the stem, so a hormone that lengthens stems is literally lengthening the storage tank.

Now cytokinins. They are adenine derivatives - purine derivatives, if you prefer. The natural one is zeatin, found in maize kernels and in coconut milk. The synthetic one is kinetin. And their nature is basic - the mirror image of gibberellin's acidic.

The organising idea here is different: cytokinin's signature move is division and youth. It promotes cell division, cytokinesis. It helps overcome apical dominance, promoting lateral shoot and bud growth - so it is auxin's opponent on that particular question. And it delays leaf senescence, which has a name worth owning: the Richmond-Lang effect. The mechanism is that it mobilises nutrients and controls protein synthesis.

One more that gets asked as a one-liner: where do cytokinins live? At sites of rapid, continuous cell division. Root apices, developing shoot buds, and young fruits. Which makes complete sense - the division hormone sits where division happens.

<whisper>And collect the acid-base tags before we move on, because they are free marks. Gibberellins acidic. Cytokinins basic. And abscisic acid, coming next, is acidic - the name tells you. Three tags, one line.
The last two regulators, and these are the brake pedal - with one large asterisk that we have already flagged.

Look at the two panels, and look particularly at the left one. Ethylene's panel is split into a green box and a red box - promoter-like and inhibitor-like. No other hormone gets that treatment. That split is the whole reason ethylene is awkward to classify, and the exam knows it.

Ethylene first. Its formula is C two H four, and it is a gaseous hormone - the only one in the list. That single fact answers a lot of one-mark questions. It is synthesised from the amino acid methionine, and supplied commercially as ethephon, which releases ethylene once it is inside the tissue.

Its effects, starting with the famous one. It hastens fruit ripening - and note the technical word, climacteric, meaning it raises the respiration rate as the fruit ripens. It promotes senescence and abscission of leaves and flowers. It breaks seed and bud dormancy. And it promotes root-hair formation. Look back at the panel and notice how those distribute across the green and red boxes - ripening and root hairs on the promoter side, senescence and abscission on the inhibitor side.

More ethylene, and these are the commercial ones. It induces flowering and synchronises fruit-set in pineapple and mango. It increases the number of female flowers in cucurbits - which matters, because female flowers are the ones that become fruit. And it is used for fruit thinning in cotton, cherry and walnut.

Now abscisic acid. Chemically it is a carotenoid derivative, and its precursor is violaxanthin. It has two other names you should recognise on sight: abscisin two, and dormin - and there is a story behind those two names that we will get to shortly. Its nature is acidic, and its identity in one phrase: the general stress hormone.

Its effects follow from that identity. It promotes seed and bud dormancy - stress says wait. And it induces stomatal closure under water stress. Look at the mechanism in the picture, because it is a favourite: A B A accumulates in drought-stressed leaves, it makes the guard cells lose turgor, so the stomata shut, and water is conserved. It also inhibits growth and metabolism generally. Everything A B A does is a plant deciding to sit this one out.

And the pairing to lock in: A B A is antagonistic to gibberellin. G A breaks dormancy, A B A enforces it. Do not learn those as two separate facts - learn them as one tug-of-war, because that is how assertion-reason questions will hand them to you.

<whisper>Now the misconception, and it is planted right in the name. Abscisic acid does not mainly cause abscission. Despite what the word suggests, abscission owes more to the ethylene and auxin balance. A B A's headline jobs are dormancy and stomatal closure. The name is a historical accident, and the examiners know you were misled by it.

This is the most-asked experiment in the subtopic, and I want to teach it as a chain of reasoning rather than a story with names attached. Each step earns the next one. If you can rebuild the chain, you can never lose the marks.
Follow the diagram left to right. Observation, inference, test, conclusion. Four boxes. That is the whole shape of good science, and it is also the shape of the answer.

Step one, the observation. Charles Darwin and his son Francis noticed that grass coleoptiles bend towards light. That alone is not interesting - everyone knew plants lean toward windows. What they did next is the interesting part: they covered different parts of the coleoptile and watched what happened. And they found something odd. The tip is what perceives the light. Yet the bending happens lower down.

Step two, the inference, and this is the intellectual move. If the tip senses the light but the base does the bending, then something must carry the message between them. A signal must travel from the tip down to the growth zone. Notice they did not know what it was. They reasoned that it had to exist. But what kind of signal - electrical, physical, chemical?

Step three, the test, and this is Went, decades later. He cut off coleoptile tips and stood them on blocks of agar - just plain jelly. If the signal was a chemical, it should soak out of the tip and into the agar. Then he took the agar block alone, with no tip at all, and put it on a tipless coleoptile. And it bent. The jelly made it bend. That is the proof - the signal is a diffusible chemical, and that chemical is auxin.

Step four, the mechanism, and this answers the question the whole thing started with. Why does it bend at all? Light drives auxin to the shaded side. More auxin on that side means more elongation on that side. So the shaded side grows faster than the lit side, and the shoot leans over - toward the light. The bending is not the plant reaching. It is one side simply outgrowing the other.

Why this matters, beyond the marks: it is the founding experiment of plant hormone biology. It is where the idea of a chemical messenger in plants came from. And it is a perennial C B S E and N E E T favourite - not because it is hard, but because it rewards students who understand a chain of reasoning rather than a list.

One honest note on sourcing. The Darwin step is grounded directly in the chapter material. The Went step is the standard N C E R T account of the same story. Learn it as given - it is what the exam expects, and it is the version every textbook carries.

अब formal definition, और इसे धीरे पढ़ने लायक है क्योंकि इसका हर clause अपनी जगह कमाता है। Plant growth regulator है एक small organic molecule, diverse chemical composition वाला, जो trace amounts में plant growth और development को influence करता है।

Clauses को अलग-अलग देखिए। Small organic molecule - यानी न protein, न enzyme. Diverse chemical composition - वही chemical zoo, definition में ही लिखा हुआ। Trace amounts में - यानी potency. और growth तथा development को influence करना - यानी job. फिर classification: दो functional groups. Promoters, यानी auxins, gibberellins और cytokinins. Inhibitors, यानी abscisic acid, और ethylene अपने inhibitory roles में।

<curious>और एक राहत, जिसे मैं साफ़ कहना चाहती हूँ क्योंकि students सबसे बुरे की उम्मीद लेकर आते हैं। P G Rs में कोई formulae नहीं, कोई dimensions नहीं। ये पूरा subtopic descriptive है। तो यहाँ equations मत ढूँढिए - हैं ही नहीं। Test ये हो रहा है कि हर molecule करता क्या है, और क्यों।
तो regulator number one: auxins. Card देखिए। चार compartments - natural, synthetic, transport, और effects - और exam का हर सवाल इन्हीं में से किसी एक में रहता है।

Auxins indole compounds हैं। Natural हैं I A A, यानी indole-three-acetic acid, और I B A, indole-three-butyric acid. Synthetic हैं N A A, naphthalene acetic acid, फिर two four D - पूरा नाम two, four-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid - और two, four, five-T. और picture में pattern notice कीजिए: दोनों natural वालों के नाम में indole है। Synthetic वालों में नहीं। यही आपका mnemonic है, और मुफ़्त है।

अब transport, और यहाँ auxin अलग है। ये एक characteristic polar तरीक़े से चलता है। Polar यानी one-way - shoot tip से base की तरफ़, और वापस नहीं। यही one-way street apical dominance को मुमकिन बनाती है, क्योंकि इसी से tip का auxin नीचे के buds तक पहुँचता है।

अब effects, और इन्हें list नहीं, एक कहानी की तरह पढ़िए। Cell elongation. Apical dominance, lateral buds को suppress करना - जो अभी किया। Stem cuttings में root initiation. ये xylem differentiation promote करता है। और ये phototropism mediate करता है, यानी light की तरफ़ झुकना।

दो और, और पहला एक trap है। Auxin young leaves और fruits का abscission रोकता है - पर पुराने वालों का गिरना promote करता है। वही hormone, उलटे outcomes, और फ़ैसला organ की उम्र से। यही पिछले section वाला context rule है, ठोस रूप में। और आख़िर में ये parthenocarpy induce करता है - बिना बीज वाला fruit जैसे tomato, dilute I A A या I B A से।

Headline application, और ये worked example में लौटेगा: two four D एक selective weedicide है, broad-leaved dicot weeds के ख़िलाफ़। Selective शब्द notice कीजिए। ये सब कुछ नहीं मारता - और crop को क्यों बख़्श देता है, ये अपने आप में एक सवाल है।
दो और promoters, और मैं इन्हें जोड़े में पढ़ाना चाहती हूँ, क्योंकि exam लगभग हमेशा इन्हें साथ test करता है और क्योंकि इनके jobs overlap नहीं करते, बल्कि एक दूसरे के पूरक हैं।

दोनों panels देखिए। बाएँ gibberellins. दाएँ cytokinins. Notice कीजिए दोनों panels में वही चार rows हैं - chemistry, nature, effects, uses. वही ढाँचा, अलग गूदा। एक card की shape सीख ली, तो दूसरा भर सकते हैं।
पहले gibberellins. ये terpene-based हैं, और सबसे ज़्यादा पढ़ा गया है G A three. इनकी nature acidic है - और ये असली exam detail है, decoration नहीं, क्योंकि acid-base tags सीधे पूछे जाते हैं।

अब effects, और organising idea ये है: gibberellin का signature move है चीज़ों को लंबा करना। Internode elongation core है, और उसी से bolting होती है - rosette plants में flowering से पहले तेज़ stem elongation. छोटा diagram देखिए: बाएँ बैठी हुई rosette, और G A three के बाद, लंबा bolted stem. ये genetic dwarfs को tall बना देता है। ये seed और bud dormancy तोड़ता है, और seed germination promote करता है। Conifers में early seed production तेज़ करता है। और germinating cereal grains में alpha-amylase synthesis induce करता है।

Applications उसी एक idea से सीधे निकलती हैं - लंबा। ये grape stalks की length बढ़ाता है। Fruit बड़ा करता है, जैसे apple. और sugarcane yield बढ़ाता है - और सोचिए ये काम क्यों करता है। Sugarcane अपनी sugar stem में store करता है, तो जो hormone stems लंबे करता है, वो literally storage tank लंबा कर रहा है।

अब cytokinins. ये adenine derivatives हैं - purine derivatives कहिए तो भी ठीक। Natural है zeatin, जो maize kernels और coconut milk में मिलता है। Synthetic है kinetin. और इनकी nature basic है - gibberellin के acidic का ठीक उल्टा।

यहाँ organising idea अलग है: cytokinin का signature move है division और जवानी। ये cell division promote करता है, cytokinesis. ये apical dominance को overcome करने में मदद करता है, lateral shoot और bud growth बढ़ा कर - यानी उस ख़ास सवाल पर ये auxin का विरोधी है। और ये leaf senescence delay करता है, जिसका नाम रखने लायक है: Richmond-Lang effect. Mechanism ये कि वो nutrients mobilise करता है और protein synthesis control करता है।

एक और जो one-liner की तरह पूछा जाता है: cytokinins रहते कहाँ हैं? तेज़, लगातार cell division की जगहों पर। Root apices, developing shoot buds, और young fruits. और ये पूरी तरह समझ आता है - division वाला hormone वहीं बैठा है जहाँ division होता है।

<whisper>और आगे बढ़ने से पहले acid-base tags समेट लीजिए, क्योंकि ये मुफ़्त marks हैं। Gibberellins acidic. Cytokinins basic. और abscisic acid, जो अगला है, acidic - नाम ही बता रहा है। तीन tags, एक line.
आख़िरी दो regulators, और यही brake pedal हैं - एक बड़े asterisk के साथ, जिसे हम पहले ही flag कर चुके हैं।

दोनों panels देखिए, और ख़ास तौर पर बायाँ। Ethylene का panel एक green box और एक red box में बँटा है - promoter-like और inhibitor-like. किसी और hormone को ये सुलूक नहीं मिला। वही बँटवारा पूरी वजह है कि ethylene को classify करना मुश्किल है, और exam ये जानता है।

पहले ethylene. इसका formula है C two H four, और ये एक gaseous hormone है - list में इकलौता। यही एक fact बहुत सारे one-mark questions का जवाब है। ये amino acid methionine से synthesise होता है, और commercially ethephon के रूप में दिया जाता है, जो tissue के अंदर पहुँच कर ethylene release करता है।

अब effects, मशहूर वाले से शुरू। ये fruit ripening तेज़ करता है - और technical word notice कीजिए, climacteric, यानी पकते वक़्त respiration rate बढ़ जाती है। ये leaves और flowers का senescence और abscission promote करता है। ये seed और bud dormancy तोड़ता है। और root-hair formation promote करता है। Panel पर वापस देखिए कि ये सब green और red boxes में कैसे बँटते हैं - ripening और root hairs promoter side, senescence और abscission inhibitor side.

और ethylene, और ये commercial वाले हैं। ये pineapple और mango में flowering induce करता है और fruit-set synchronise करता है। ये cucurbits में female flowers की संख्या बढ़ाता है - जो मायने रखता है, क्योंकि female flowers ही fruit बनते हैं। और cotton, cherry तथा walnut में fruit thinning के लिए इस्तेमाल होता है।

अब abscisic acid. Chemically ये carotenoid derivative है, और इसका precursor है violaxanthin. इसके दो और नाम हैं जो देखते ही पहचान लेने चाहिए: abscisin two, और dormin - और इन दो नामों के पीछे एक कहानी है जिस तक हम जल्द पहुँचेंगे। इसकी nature acidic है, और एक phrase में इसकी पहचान: the general stress hormone.

इसके effects उसी पहचान से निकलते हैं। ये seed और bud dormancy promote करता है - stress कहता है रुको। और water stress में stomatal closure induce करता है। Picture में mechanism देखिए, क्योंकि ये favourite है: A B A drought-stressed leaves में जमा होता है, guard cells का turgor छीन लेता है, तो stomata बंद, और पानी बचा। ये growth और metabolism को आम तौर पर inhibit भी करता है। A B A जो कुछ करता है वो plant का ये तय करना है कि इस दौर को बैठ कर निकालना है।

और lock करने वाली जोड़ी: A B A gibberellin का antagonist है। G A dormancy तोड़ता है, A B A उसे लागू करता है। इन्हें दो अलग facts की तरह मत सीखिए - एक रस्साकशी की तरह सीखिए, क्योंकि assertion-reason questions इन्हें इसी शक्ल में देंगे।

<whisper>अब misconception, और वो नाम में ही बोया हुआ है। Abscisic acid मुख्य रूप से abscission नहीं कराता। शब्द चाहे जो इशारा करे, abscission ज़्यादातर ethylene और auxin के balance से होता है। A B A के headline jobs हैं dormancy और stomatal closure. नाम एक historical हादसा है, और examiners जानते हैं कि आप उससे बहके थे।

ये subtopic का सबसे ज़्यादा पूछा जाने वाला experiment है, और मैं इसे नामों वाली कहानी की तरह नहीं, reasoning की एक chain की तरह पढ़ाना चाहती हूँ। हर step अगले को कमाता है। Chain दोबारा बना सकते हैं, तो marks कभी नहीं जाएँगे।
Diagram बाएँ से दाएँ follow कीजिए। Observation, inference, test, conclusion. चार boxes. यही अच्छे science की पूरी शक्ल है, और यही answer की भी।

Step one, observation. Charles Darwin और उनके बेटे Francis ने notice किया कि grass coleoptiles light की तरफ़ मुड़ते हैं। अकेले में ये दिलचस्प नहीं - सब जानते थे कि plants खिड़की की तरफ़ झुकते हैं। दिलचस्प वो है जो उन्होंने आगे किया: उन्होंने coleoptile के अलग-अलग हिस्से ढके और देखा क्या होता है। और एक अजीब बात मिली। Light को tip perceive करता है। पर मुड़ना नीचे होता है।

Step two, inference, और यही असली बौद्धिक चाल है। अगर tip light महसूस करता है पर मुड़ना base करता है, तो कोई चीज़ दोनों के बीच संदेश ले जा रही है। कोई signal tip से नीचे growth zone तक जाता होगा। Notice कीजिए उन्हें नहीं पता था वो क्या है। उन्होंने reason किया कि उसका होना ज़रूरी है। पर किस तरह का signal - electrical, physical, chemical?

Step three, test, और ये Went हैं, दशकों बाद। उन्होंने coleoptile tips काट कर agar के blocks पर खड़ा किया - बस सादी जेली। अगर signal chemical है, तो उसे tip से रिस कर agar में उतरना चाहिए। फिर उन्होंने अकेला agar block लिया, बिना किसी tip के, और एक tipless coleoptile पर रखा। और वो मुड़ गया। जेली ने उसे मोड़ दिया। यही proof है - signal एक diffusible chemical है, और वो chemical है auxin.

Step four, mechanism, और यही उस सवाल का जवाब है जिससे सब शुरू हुआ था। मुड़ता क्यों है? Light auxin को shaded side पर धकेल देती है। उस side ज़्यादा auxin यानी उस side ज़्यादा elongation. तो shaded side, lit side से तेज़ बढ़ती है, और shoot झुक जाता है - light की तरफ़। मुड़ना plant का पहुँचना नहीं है। ये बस एक side का दूसरी से ज़्यादा बढ़ जाना है।

Marks से आगे ये क्यों मायने रखता है: ये plant hormone biology का founding experiment है। Plants में chemical messenger का idea यहीं से आया। और ये C B S E तथा N E E T का पक्का favourite है - इसलिए नहीं कि मुश्किल है, बल्कि इसलिए कि ये उन students को इनाम देता है जो list नहीं, reasoning की chain समझते हैं।

Sourcing पर एक ईमानदार note. Darwin वाला step सीधे chapter material में grounded है। Went वाला step उसी कहानी का standard N C E R T account है। जैसा दिया है वैसा सीखिए - exam यही expect करता है, और हर textbook यही version रखता है।

board_events.text: GIBBERELLIN: traced to the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi, which causes the 'foolish seedling' (bakanae) disease of rice. Infected plants grow abnormally TALL - revealing a growth-promoting chemical.

CYTOKININ: kinetin was isolated from AUTOCLAVED (degraded) herring-sperm DNA by Miller and Skoog, who were hunting for a cell-division factor. The natural counterpart, ZEATIN, was later found in maize.
ETHYLENE: the observation that ripe oranges hastened the ripening of bananas stored nearby pointed to a VOLATILE ripening signal - a gas.
ABA: found INDEPENDENTLY as a growth-inhibitor ('abscisin II') and as a dormancy-inducer ('dormin'). The two names were later merged into abscisic acid.
Pattern worth noticing: every one of these began as a nuisance, a contamination or an oddity that somebody refused to explain away.
Sourcing note: the bakanae naming and the Cousins observation are the standard N C E R T framing.
The most testable process idea in the subtopic
In a mass of undifferentiated cells - a CALLUS - the RATIO of the two hormones, not their absolute amounts, decides what the tissue builds.

board_events.text: A HIGH AUXIN : CYTOKININ ratio favours ROOT differentiation.
A HIGH CYTOKININ : AUXIN ratio favours SHOOT differentiation.
A BALANCED ratio keeps the callus dividing WITHOUT organising into either organ.

Why a ratio, and not the totals? Because the two hormones act ANTAGONISTICALLY on the same developmental programme. The cell reads their RELATIVE levels as a coordinate that tells it which organ to build.
Memory hook: 'Roots need Auxin, Shoots need Cytokinin - the bigger partner wins.'
This is the single most repeated N E E T concept in the subtopic. Lock the direction and never guess it.
Measure a hormone by what it DOES
Since hormones act in trace amounts, they cannot simply be weighed out. They are quantified by a BIOLOGICAL RESPONSE - a bioassay.

GIBBERELLIN: the dwarf pea / dwarf corn ELONGATION test - the dwarfs grow tall in proportion to the GA applied.
CYTOKININ: the cell-division / callus-growth test.
ANTAGONISMS: ABA opposes gibberellin (dormancy vs germination). Cytokinin opposes ethylene (anti-senescence vs senescence), and partly opposes auxin (lateral-bud release vs apical dominance).
These push-pull pairs are exactly where N E E T sets its assertion-reason traps. Every antagonism is two opposite answers to ONE question.
Every application is a function, pointed at a goal

board_events.text: AUXINS root stem cuttings in nurseries - IBA and NAA are the rooting hormones of choice. They produce seedless parthenocarpic fruit such as tomato from dilute IAA or IBA. And as 2,4-D, they clear dicot weeds from cereal lawns and fields.
GIBBERELLINS lengthen the stalk and enlarge the fruit of grapes, increase the yield of sugarcane (which stores its sugar in the stem), and hasten maturity in young conifers.
GA also speeds the malting of barley by inducing alpha-amylase - which is why gibberellin matters to the brewing industry.
CYTOKININS extend the shelf life of vegetables and cut flowers by holding off senescence.

ETHYLENE, usually applied as ethephon, ripens and de-greens fruit on demand, synchronises fruit-set and induces flowering in pineapple, promotes female flowers (and hence yield) in cucurbits, and thins excess fruit in cotton, cherry and walnut.
The throughline: pick the hormone whose natural job IS the outcome the grower wants. Nothing here is a new fact - it is the function list, aimed at money.

segments.text: Four more discoveries, and the chapter deliberately gives them to you in one breath. But do not let that make them feel like trivia - each one is a short argument, and each one gets asked.
Look at the four quadrants. A diseased rice plant, a jar of degraded D N A, some oranges next to bananas, and two old names being merged. Four unglamorous starting points.

Gibberellin first. It was traced to a fungus - Gibberella fujikuroi - which causes the foolish seedling disease of rice, called bakanae. Look at the little pair in the picture: the healthy plant on the left, the infected one towering over it. Now think about how strange that is. A disease that makes the crop grow taller. The infected plants grow abnormally tall, and that is the clue - if infection makes plants tall, the fungus must be making a growth-promoting chemical. The disease was the assay.

Cytokinin next, and this one is my favourite for how accidental it was. Miller and Skoog were hunting for a cell-division factor. They found their answer in autoclaved herring-sperm D N A - that is, D N A that had been cooked and degraded. The active substance was not the D N A itself; it was a breakdown product. They called it kinetin. The natural counterpart, zeatin, was found later, in maize.

Ethylene, and this one you could have discovered in a kitchen. Somebody noticed that ripe oranges hastened the ripening of bananas stored nearby. Nothing touched. Nothing was passed between them except air. So the signal had to be volatile - it had to be a gas. That is the entire inference, and it is correct.

And abscisic acid, whose story explains those two extra names from the last section. It was found independently, by different people, twice. One group found a growth-inhibitor and named it abscisin two. Another found a dormancy-inducer and named it dormin. It was the same molecule wearing two coats. The two names were later merged into abscisic acid - which is why you must recognise all three.

<curious>Now step back and notice the pattern, because it is worth more than the four facts. Every one of these began as a nuisance, a contamination or an oddity. A crop disease. Cooked D N A. Fruit spoiling too fast. Somebody refused to explain the annoyance away, and asked why instead. That is the whole method.

And the sourcing note, kept honest as always. The bakanae naming and the Cousins observation on oranges and bananas are the standard N C E R T framing of these discoveries. Learn them as given - that is the version the paper will use.

<excited>Now the idea I promised you in section one, and it is the most testable process in this entire subtopic. This is where the balance principle stops being a slogan and becomes a switch you can throw.

Here is the setup. Take a callus - a mass of undifferentiated cells, no roots, no shoots, no organisation, just cells. Now feed it hormones and watch what it builds. And here is the punchline, which I want you to hear before the details: what decides the outcome is the ratio of the two hormones, not their absolute amounts.
Look at the three flasks. Same callus in each. The only difference is the ratio in the box above it. Three ratios, three completely different outcomes.

Flask one: a high auxin-to-cytokinin ratio. Auxin dominates. And the callus builds roots. Look at the picture - roots differentiate out of a formless lump, simply because one hormone outnumbered the other.

Flask two: flip it. A high cytokinin-to-auxin ratio. Cytokinin dominates. And now the same callus builds shoots instead. Nothing else changed. Same cells, same genes, same flask. Only the ratio was reversed, and the organ reversed with it.

Flask three: balance the two. And now something interesting happens - nothing organises at all. The callus keeps dividing, growing as a lump, without becoming either roots or shoots. So a balanced ratio is not a compromise organ. It is no organ. The switch has to be thrown one way or the other for anything to be built.

Now the question worth asking, because this is what separates understanding from memorising. Why a ratio, and not the totals? Because the two hormones act antagonistically on the same developmental programme. They are pulling on the same rope, in opposite directions. So the cell cannot read either one alone and learn anything useful. What it can read is their relative levels - and it reads that as a coordinate, a position that tells it which organ to build.

The memory hook from the chapter, and say it out loud: roots need auxin, shoots need cytokinin - the bigger partner wins. Roots and auxin, shoots and cytokinin. Whichever hormone is bigger, its organ is what you get.

<whisper>And I will be blunt about the stakes. This is the single most repeated N E E T concept in the subtopic. It comes up almost every year, and its strongest distractor is always the exact reversal - roots where shoots should be. So lock the direction now, and never, ever guess it in the hall.

A short but heavily-tested section, and it begins with a practical problem. Hormones act in trace amounts. A few molecules can swing an organ. So how on earth do you measure how much is there? You cannot weigh it out on a balance - there is not enough of it to weigh.

The answer is elegant: measure the hormone by what it does. Give it to a plant, and read the size of the response. If the response is proportional to the dose, the plant becomes your measuring instrument. That is a bioassay - a biological assay - and the chapter gives you three.
Look at the three panels along the top. One per hormone, and each is just a response with a ruler held against it.

Auxin: the Avena coleoptile curvature test. You apply auxin to one side of a coleoptile and it bends. And here is the part that makes it an assay rather than a demonstration - the degree of bending is proportional to the auxin present. More auxin, more bend. So you read the angle and you have your answer.

Gibberellin: the dwarf pea or dwarf corn elongation test. Take a genetic dwarf - a plant that is short because it cannot make enough G A. Apply gibberellin, and it grows tall. Look at the three stems in the panel, each taller than the last. The dwarfs grow tall in proportion to the G A applied. The height is the reading.

Cytokinin: the cell-division test, also called the callus-growth test. Cytokinin's signature job is division, so you measure division. More cytokinin, more cells. Notice the logic across all three: each assay uses the hormone's own signature effect as the ruler. That is why you can reconstruct the list rather than memorise it.

Now antagonisms, and this is the other half of the section. A B A opposes gibberellin - dormancy against germination. Cytokinin opposes ethylene - anti-senescence against senescence. And cytokinin partly opposes auxin - lateral-bud release against apical dominance. Three pairs, and notice each pair is two opposite answers to one single question. Should this seed wait or sprout? Should this leaf hold on or let go? Should this bud grow or stay quiet?

<whisper>And here is why I am spending time on this. These push-pull pairs are exactly where N E E T sets its assertion-reason traps. The question will give you one hormone's effect as the assertion and its opponent's as the reason, and see whether you can hold both directions straight. If you learn each antagonism as a single tug-of-war rather than two loose facts, those traps stop working on you.

This section looks like the longest list in the chapter, and students dread it. So let me hand you the shortcut first: there is nothing new here. Not one new fact. Every single application is a function you already learned, pointed at something a farmer wants to sell.
Look at the four blocks. One per hormone, each with its uses stacked beside it. As I go through them, do not memorise the line - ask yourself which effect from earlier is being cashed in.

Auxins. They root stem cuttings in nurseries - I B A and N A A are the rooting hormones of choice. Which effect is that? Root initiation in stem cuttings. Straight from the auxin card. They produce seedless parthenocarpic fruit, such as tomato, from dilute I A A or I B A - that is parthenocarpy, also straight from the card. And as two four D, they clear dicot weeds from cereal lawns and fields.

Gibberellins, and the theme is the one we set earlier: longer. They lengthen the stalk and enlarge the fruit of grapes. They increase the yield of sugarcane - and remember why that works, because sugarcane stores its sugar in the stem, so a longer stem is a bigger tank. And they hasten maturity in young conifers.

One more gibberellin use, and this one is worth its own line because it surprises people. G A speeds the malting of barley by inducing alpha-amylase. Alpha-amylase breaks starch into sugar. Sugar is what gets fermented. Which is why gibberellin matters to the brewing industry - a plant hormone with a place in a brewery, all because of one enzyme on the effects list.

Cytokinins get one line, and it is a direct cash-in of the Richmond-Lang effect. They extend the shelf life of vegetables and cut flowers by holding off senescence. The hormone that delays leaf ageing is sold to keep bouquets fresh.

Ethylene, usually applied as ethephon. It ripens and de-greens fruit on demand. It synchronises fruit-set and induces flowering in pineapple. It promotes female flowers - and hence yield - in cucurbits. And it thins excess fruit in cotton, cherry and walnut. Four uses, and every one of them was on the ethylene effects list ten minutes ago.

So the throughline, and this is what to carry into the exam. Pick the hormone whose natural job is the outcome the grower wants. If the question asks how to get a cutting to root, ask which hormone's natural job is rooting. You are not recalling an applications list - you are reading the functions backwards.
चार और discoveries, और chapter जानबूझ कर इन्हें एक साँस में देता है। पर इससे इन्हें trivia मत समझिए - हर एक एक छोटी दलील है, और हर एक पूछी जाती है।
चारों quadrants देखिए। एक बीमार rice plant, degraded D N A का एक जार, bananas के बगल में कुछ oranges, और दो पुराने नाम मिलते हुए। चार बेरौनक़ शुरुआतें।

पहले gibberellin. इसे एक fungus तक traced किया गया - Gibberella fujikuroi - जो rice की foolish seedling disease करता है, जिसे bakanae कहते हैं। Picture में छोटी जोड़ी देखिए: बाएँ healthy plant, दाएँ infected वाला उससे ऊँचा। अब सोचिए ये कितना अजीब है। एक बीमारी जो फ़सल को लंबा कर देती है। Infected plants असामान्य रूप से tall बढ़ते हैं, और वही सुराग़ है - अगर infection plants को लंबा करता है, तो fungus कोई growth-promoting chemical बना रहा होगा। बीमारी ही assay थी।

अब cytokinin, और ये मुझे सबसे प्यारा लगता है कि कितना accidental था। Miller और Skoog एक cell-division factor ढूँढ रहे थे। जवाब मिला autoclaved herring-sperm D N A में - यानी वो D N A जो पका कर degrade कर दिया गया था। Active substance ख़ुद D N A नहीं था; वो एक breakdown product था। उन्होंने उसे kinetin कहा। Natural counterpart, zeatin, बाद में मिला, maize में।

Ethylene, और ये आप रसोई में खोज सकते थे। किसी ने notice किया कि पके oranges पास रखे bananas का पकना तेज़ कर देते हैं। कुछ छुआ नहीं। उनके बीच हवा के सिवा कुछ गया नहीं। तो signal volatile ही होगा - gas ही होगा। यही पूरी inference है, और सही है।

और abscisic acid, जिसकी कहानी पिछले section वाले दो अतिरिक्त नाम समझा देती है। इसे अलग-अलग लोगों ने, स्वतंत्र रूप से, दो बार खोजा। एक group को growth-inhibitor मिला और उन्होंने नाम रखा abscisin two. दूसरे को dormancy-inducer मिला और नाम रखा dormin. वो एक ही molecule था, दो कोट पहने हुए। बाद में दोनों नाम मिला कर abscisic acid बना - इसीलिए तीनों पहचानने ज़रूरी हैं।

<curious>अब पीछे हट कर pattern notice कीजिए, क्योंकि वो इन चार facts से ज़्यादा क़ीमती है। इनमें से हर एक की शुरुआत एक झंझट, एक contamination या एक अजीब बात से हुई। फ़सल की बीमारी। पका हुआ D N A. Fruit का जल्दी ख़राब होना। किसी ने उस खीझ को टालने से इनकार किया, और पूछा कि क्यों। यही पूरा method है।

और sourcing note, हमेशा की तरह ईमानदार। Bakanae का नाम और oranges-bananas वाली Cousins observation इन discoveries की standard N C E R T framing हैं। जैसा दिया है वैसा सीखिए - paper यही version इस्तेमाल करेगा।

<excited>अब वो idea जिसका section one में वादा किया था, और ये इस पूरे subtopic का सबसे testable process है। यहीं balance principle slogan होना बंद करता है और एक switch बन जाता है जिसे आप दबा सकते हैं।

Setup ये है। एक callus लीजिए - undifferentiated cells का ढेर, न roots, न shoots, न कोई organisation, बस cells. अब उसे hormones खिलाइए और देखिए वो बनाता क्या है। और punchline पहले सुन लीजिए, details से पहले: outcome तय करता है दोनों hormones का ratio, उनकी absolute amounts नहीं।
तीनों flasks देखिए। हर एक में वही callus. फ़र्क सिर्फ़ ऊपर वाले box में लिखा ratio है। तीन ratios, तीन बिलकुल अलग outcomes.
Flask one: high auxin-to-cytokinin ratio. Auxin हावी है। और callus roots बनाता है। Picture देखिए - एक बेशक्ल लोंदे से roots differentiate हो रहे हैं, सिर्फ़ इसलिए कि एक hormone दूसरे से ज़्यादा था।

Flask two: उलट दीजिए। High cytokinin-to-auxin ratio. Cytokinin हावी है। और अब वही callus shoots बनाता है। और कुछ नहीं बदला। वही cells, वही genes, वही flask. सिर्फ़ ratio उलटा, और उसके साथ organ भी उलट गया।

Flask three: दोनों बराबर कर दीजिए। और अब दिलचस्प बात - कुछ organise होता ही नहीं। Callus divide करता रहता है, लोंदे की तरह बढ़ता रहता है, न roots बनता है न shoots. यानी balanced ratio कोई बीच का organ नहीं है। वो कोई organ नहीं है। कुछ भी बनने के लिए switch को एक तरफ़ दबाना ही पड़ेगा।

अब पूछने लायक सवाल, क्योंकि यही समझने और रटने का फ़र्क है। Ratio क्यों, totals क्यों नहीं? क्योंकि दोनों hormones एक ही developmental programme पर antagonistically काम करते हैं। वो एक ही रस्सी को उलटी दिशाओं में खींच रहे हैं। तो cell किसी एक को अकेले पढ़ कर कुछ काम की बात नहीं जान सकता। वो जो पढ़ सकता है वो है उनके relative levels - और उसे वो एक coordinate की तरह पढ़ता है, एक position जो बताती है कौन सा organ बनाना है।
Chapter का memory hook, और इसे ज़ोर से बोलिए: roots need auxin, shoots need cytokinin - the bigger partner wins. Roots और auxin, shoots और cytokinin. जो hormone बड़ा, उसी का organ मिलेगा।

<whisper>और दाँव पर क्या है, ये मैं सीधे कहूँगी। ये इस subtopic का सबसे ज़्यादा दोहराया जाने वाला N E E T concept है। ये लगभग हर साल आता है, और इसका सबसे मज़बूत distractor हमेशा ठीक उल्टा होता है - जहाँ shoots चाहिए वहाँ roots. तो direction अभी lock कीजिए, और hall में कभी, कभी भी इसका अंदाज़ा मत लगाइए।

एक छोटा पर भारी test होने वाला section, और शुरुआत एक practical मुश्किल से। Hormones trace amounts में काम करते हैं। चंद molecules पूरा organ पलट सकते हैं। तो आख़िर आप नापेंगे कैसे कि कितना है? Balance पर तौल नहीं सकते - तौलने लायक है ही नहीं।

जवाब ख़ूबसूरत है: hormone को इस बात से नापिए कि वो करता क्या है। Plant को दीजिए, और response का size पढ़िए। अगर response dose के proportional है, तो plant ख़ुद आपका measuring instrument बन गया। यही bioassay है - biological assay - और chapter आपको तीन देता है।
ऊपर के तीनों panels देखिए। हर hormone के लिए एक, और हर एक बस एक response है जिस पर scale लगी है।

Auxin: Avena coleoptile curvature test. आप coleoptile की एक side auxin लगाते हैं और वो मुड़ जाता है। और यही हिस्सा इसे demonstration से assay बनाता है - मुड़ने की मात्रा मौजूद auxin के proportional है। ज़्यादा auxin, ज़्यादा मोड़। तो आप angle पढ़िए और जवाब हाज़िर।

Gibberellin: dwarf pea या dwarf corn elongation test. एक genetic dwarf लीजिए - वो plant जो छोटा है क्योंकि पर्याप्त G A नहीं बना पाता। Gibberellin लगाइए, और वो लंबा हो जाता है। Panel में तीन stems देखिए, हर अगला पिछले से ऊँचा। Dwarfs लगाए गए G A के proportional लंबे होते हैं। Height ही reading है।

Cytokinin: cell-division test, जिसे callus-growth test भी कहते हैं। Cytokinin का signature job है division, तो आप division नापते हैं। ज़्यादा cytokinin, ज़्यादा cells. तीनों में logic notice कीजिए: हर assay उसी hormone के अपने signature effect को scale बनाता है। इसीलिए आप ये list रट नहीं, बना सकते हैं।

अब antagonisms, और यही section का दूसरा आधा है। A B A gibberellin का विरोधी - dormancy बनाम germination. Cytokinin ethylene का विरोधी - anti-senescence बनाम senescence. और cytokinin आंशिक रूप से auxin का विरोधी - lateral-bud release बनाम apical dominance. तीन जोड़ियाँ, और notice कीजिए हर जोड़ी एक ही सवाल के दो उलटे जवाब है। ये seed रुके या उगे? ये leaf टिके या गिरे? ये bud बढ़े या चुप रहे?

<whisper>और मैं इस पर वक़्त क्यों दे रही हूँ। यही push-pull जोड़ियाँ हैं जहाँ N E E T अपने assertion-reason traps बिछाता है। Question एक hormone का effect assertion में देगा और उसके विरोधी का reason में, और देखेगा कि आप दोनों directions सीधी रख पाते हैं या नहीं। हर antagonism को दो ढीले facts की जगह एक रस्साकशी की तरह सीख लीजिए, तो वो traps आप पर काम करना बंद कर देंगे।

ये section chapter की सबसे लंबी list लगता है, और students इससे डरते हैं। तो पहले shortcut पकड़ लीजिए: यहाँ कुछ भी नया नहीं है। एक भी नया fact नहीं। हर application वो function है जो आप पहले पढ़ चुके हैं, बस किसी ऐसी चीज़ पर तान दिया गया जो किसान बेचना चाहता है।
चारों blocks देखिए। हर hormone के लिए एक, और बगल में uses. जैसे-जैसे मैं चलूँ, line रटिए मत - ख़ुद से पूछिए कि पहले वाला कौन सा effect यहाँ भुनाया जा रहा है।

Auxins. ये nurseries में stem cuttings को root कराते हैं - I B A और N A A rooting hormones of choice हैं। ये कौन सा effect है? Stem cuttings में root initiation. सीधे auxin card से। ये बिना बीज वाला parthenocarpic fruit बनाते हैं, जैसे tomato, dilute I A A या I B A से - वो parthenocarpy है, वो भी सीधे card से। और two four D की शक्ल में, ये cereal lawns और खेतों से dicot weeds साफ़ करते हैं।

Gibberellins, और theme वही है जो पहले तय किया: लंबा। ये grapes का stalk लंबा करते हैं और fruit बड़ा। ये sugarcane की yield बढ़ाते हैं - और याद रखिए क्यों, क्योंकि sugarcane अपनी sugar stem में रखता है, तो लंबा stem यानी बड़ा tank. और ये young conifers में maturity जल्दी लाते हैं।

एक और gibberellin use, और ये अपनी अलग line का हक़दार है क्योंकि ये लोगों को चौंकाता है। G A barley की malting तेज़ करता है, alpha-amylase induce करके। Alpha-amylase starch को sugar में तोड़ता है। Sugar ही ferment होती है। इसीलिए gibberellin brewing industry के लिए मायने रखता है - एक plant hormone की brewery में जगह, सिर्फ़ effects list के एक enzyme की वजह से।

Cytokinins को एक line मिलती है, और वो Richmond-Lang effect का सीधा भुनाना है। ये vegetables और cut flowers की shelf life बढ़ाते हैं, senescence रोक कर। जो hormone leaf ageing delay करता है, वो bouquets ताज़ा रखने के लिए बिकता है।

Ethylene, आम तौर पर ethephon के रूप में। ये माँग पर fruit पकाता और de-green करता है। Pineapple में fruit-set synchronise करता है और flowering induce करता है। Cucurbits में female flowers - और इसलिए yield - बढ़ाता है। और cotton, cherry तथा walnut में ज़्यादा fruit thin करता है। चार uses, और हर एक दस मिनट पहले ethylene की effects list पर था।

तो throughline, और यही exam में ले जाना है। वो hormone चुनिए जिसका natural job वही outcome है जो grower चाहता है। Question पूछे कि cutting को root कैसे कराएँ, तो पूछिए किस hormone का natural job rooting है। आप applications list याद नहीं कर रहे - आप functions को उल्टा पढ़ रहे हैं।

board_events.text: (a) closure of stomata during water stress. Clue word: STRESS. Answer - ABSCISIC ACID, the stress hormone; it closes stomata to conserve water.
(b) ripening of climacteric fruits. Clue word: RIPENING. Answer - ETHYLENE, the gaseous ripening hormone, supplied commercially as ethephon.
(c) bolting in rosette plants. Clue word: BOLTING. Answer - GIBBERELLIN; it drives internode elongation, hence bolting.
(d) overcoming apical dominance to promote lateral buds. Clue: OVERCOMING apical dominance. Answer - CYTOKININ; it promotes lateral bud growth, antagonising auxin's apical dominance.
Answer: (a) ABA, (b) ethylene, (c) gibberellin, (d) cytokinin.
C B S E tip: one clean line per part, hormone named FIRST, then the one-phrase reason. Do not write a paragraph where a line scores full marks.

board_events.text: Column I: A. 2,4-D. B. Gibberellin (GA3). C. Cytokinin. D. Ethephon.
Column II: i. Hastening fruit ripening. ii. Killing broad-leaved weeds. iii. Lengthening grape and sugarcane stalk. iv. Delaying senescence of cut flowers.
A: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin weedicide, lethal to broad-leaved dicots. So A matches ii.
B: GA3 elongates internodes, so it lengthens stalks - grape and sugarcane. B matches iii.
C: Cytokinin postpones senescence - the Richmond-Lang effect - and so keeps cut flowers fresh. C matches iv.
D: Ethephon releases ethylene in the tissue, and ethylene is the ripening gas. D matches i.
Answer: A-ii, B-iii, C-iv, D-i.
N E E T: predict the outcome in each flask
A callus is divided into three flasks. Flask 1 is given a high auxin-to-cytokinin ratio. Flask 2 a high cytokinin-to-auxin ratio. Flask 3 a balanced ratio. Predict the outcome in each.

board_events.text: The governing principle: the organ a callus builds is set by the RATIO, not by the totals.
Flask 1 - auxin-dominant. ROOTS differentiate.
Flask 2 - cytokinin-dominant. SHOOTS differentiate.
Flask 3 - balanced. The callus keeps dividing WITHOUT organising into roots or shoots.
Answer: Flask 1 gives roots; Flask 2 gives shoots; Flask 3 gives undifferentiated callus growth.
This ratio is the single most repeated N E E T concept in the subtopic - and its strongest distractor is always the exact reversal.
N E E T high-difficulty: assertion and reason
ASSERTION (A): 2,4-D is used to clear dicot weeds from a field of wheat without harming the crop.
REASON (R): 2,4-D, a synthetic auxin, is far more lethal to broad-leaved dicots than to narrow-leaved monocots like wheat.
